contentBlocks.text: Letters make sounds, and sounds build words! Today we're meeting one letter and its sound: S. The letter S makes a hissing sound, like air escaping from a balloon: sss.

Say 'sss' together and notice how your tongue sits just behind your teeth. Now try some words that start with that sound: sun, snake, sock, soap. Say each word slowly and stretch out the very first sound: sss-un, sss-nake, sss-ock, sss-oap. Can you think of one more word that starts with the S sound?
Great listening! Every time you hear that hissing 'sss' sound at the start of a word, you'll know it probably starts with the letter S.

objectives: Identify the letter S and produce its most common sound (/s/)
Recognize the /s/ sound at the beginning of familiar words
materialsNeeded: Optional: a few small objects starting with S (sock, spoon, sticker) for a sorting game
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Show the letter S and model its sound: 'sss', like a snake or air escaping a balloon.
2. Say the sound together five times, exaggerating the hiss.
3. Say a list of words slowly, stretching the first sound: sun, snake, sock, soap. Ask the child to give a thumbs up when they hear the /s/ sound at the start.
4. Play a quick sorting game if you have small objects handy: does this word start with /s/ or not?
5. Move to the worksheet: trace the letter S, then practice writing it once more.
6. Close by brainstorming one more S word together.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus only on hearing the sound (no writing yet) — clapping or tapping the table each time they hear /s/ at the start of a word
Ready for more: ask the child to think of an S word for each letter of a short list of categories (an animal, a food, a color-adjacent word)
For a child who already writes letters confidently, have them write a full row of S's from memory before tracing
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and sound-recognition activity — there is no right/wrong answer beyond correct letter formation and hearing the /s/ sound.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Letter-sound correspondence (phonemic awareness) is the foundational Kindergarten ELA skill every later decoding and reading-fluency skill builds on.

generationData.instructions: Trace each letter, say its sound out loud, then write it once more on your own.

rows.label: Capital S — say 'sss', like a snake
Lowercase s — same sound, smaller letter
